scenario.title: Modernise the clearing batch: COBOL to Java 21

turns.prompt: Migrate nexus-payments/legacy/clearing-batch/CLEARING.cbl to Java 21 under MOD-2026-07. Keep its behaviour identical: the same input must give the same report, byte for byte. Write nexus-payments/services/clearing/src/main/java/com/nexusbank/clearing/ClearingBatch.java, taking the input file and the report file as its two arguments, and a JUnit 5 characterisation test, nexus-payments/services/clearing/src/test/java/com/nexusbank/clearing/ClearingBatchCharacterisationTest.java. The tests run from the repository root, nexus-payments/: the test runs ClearingBatch on legacy/clearing-batch/clearing_input.dat, writes its report to a JUnit @TempDir and compares it with legacy/clearing-batch/expected_totals.txt by Reports.assertSameBytes(expected, actual). Use the Bank's COBOL compatibility library in libs/cobol-compat (package com.nexusbank.cobol), as MIG-004 requires, and do not write your own versions of it: FixedRecord.text and FixedRecord.decimal for each input field, CobolMath.rounded for COMPUTE ... ROUNDED, Picture.edit for every edited picture, Picture.text for every text item moved into a report line, LineSequential to read the input and write the report, and Reports.assertSameBytes to compare the two reports in the test. Pass each PICTURE exactly as the COBOL source writes it, with its column from the layouts.

rules.text:
**MIG-002 Behaviour first.** A migration MUST NOT change behaviour. The new program does what the old one does, including its rounding, its filters and its report format, even where that looks wrong. A defect found on the way, such as a comment that contradicts the code, MUST be raised as its own ticket and fixed, if at all, in a separate change, never in passing. Where a comment and the code disagree, the code is the behaviour to keep.
Traces to: TEC-POL-004 clause 4.3; TEC-POL-002 clause 4.1.

## 4. Mapping the code
**MIG-004 COBOL to Java mapping.** A Java port MUST use the COBOL compatibility library (`com.nexusbank.cobol`) for fields by PICTURE as the COBOL writes it (`FixedRecord`); `ROUNDED`, half away from zero, and truncation (`CobolMath`); edited pictures, with zero suppression, separators and a trailing minus (`Picture.edit`); and line-sequential files without trailing spaces (`LineSequential`). Never hand-write them. Money is `BigDecimal`, never `float` or `double`.
Traces to: TEC-POL-004 clause 4.3; FIN-POL-003 clause 4.3.

## 4. Migrations
**TST-010 Characterisation tests for migrations.** Before a program is migrated or rewritten, for example from COBOL to Java or Rust, or from a Java job to Python, its current behaviour MUST be captured in characterisation tests: the same inputs run through the old and the new program MUST give identical outputs, to the penny. The new program MUST NOT go live until they pass.
Traces to: FIN-POL-003 clause 4.8 (Testing of changes to systems that calculate charges).

**CLR-WIKI-019 Q1: ROUNDED rounds half away from zero.** Each fee is `COMPUTE WS-FEE ROUNDED = IN-AMOUNT * IN-FEE-RATE`, rounded on its own, then added up. A half penny goes away from zero: +0.145 is 0.15 and -0.145 is -0.15. That's `CobolMath.rounded(fee, "S9(9)V99")`, or `cobol_math::rounded` in Rust. Hand-rolled, it goes wrong: `HALF_EVEN` and `Math.round` both turn the fixture's -0.165 refund fee into -0.16, not -0.17.
Traces to: MIG-004 and MIG-005 (Legacy Modernisation Standard); PAY-012 (Payments Engineering Standard).

**PM-2024-011 L5: A rewrite is a change to money code.** Before the new version of a job replaces the old one, run both on the same inputs and prove they give the same answers. The Java job had this right for years; nobody checked that the Python one agreed with it.
Traces to: TST-010 (Testing and Definition of Done Standard).
